spacr.ml.fit_mixed_model.canonical_text:
Fit a mixed model with guides nested within genes.

The model treats genes as fixed effects and guides as random effects
nested within genes. In statsmodels notation, ``groups=gene`` supplies the
outer random intercept and ``vc_formula={'grna': '0 + C(grna)'}`` supplies
the guide-within-gene variance component.

A blockable ``screenID`` supplied by :func:`prepare_formula` remains a
fixed effect. With only two screen levels, a random screen variance would
be estimated from one degree of freedom. The plate is not nested within
the screen because plate position is already represented by the row and
column structure. Single-screen data omit the constant screen term to
avoid a rank-deficient design.

Parameters
----------
df : pandas.DataFrame
    Model data containing the formula variables and the gene and guide
    grouping columns.
formula : str
    Fixed-effects formula, normally returned by :func:`prepare_formula`
    with ``level='gene'``.
dst : path-like
    Destination for the residual histogram.
random_row_column_effects : bool, default False
    Add row and column variance components instead of fixed terms.
gene_column : str, default 'gene'
    Column containing the outer gene groups.
guide_column : str, default 'grna'
    Column containing guides nested within each gene.
regression_backend : {'statsmodels', 'torch'}, default 'statsmodels'
    Mixed-model backend. The torch backend fits the same nested model
    with GPU acceleration when available.

Returns
-------
mixed_model
    Fitted backend-specific mixed-model result.
coef_df : pandas.DataFrame
    Fixed effects, variance components, and guide BLUPs. Variance
    components and BLUPs have ``NaN`` p-values because they are not
    fixed-effect hypothesis tests. ``coef_df.attrs['mixed_fit']`` records
    which model was fitted, the optimiser that produced it, every
    fallback taken, whether it converged and which variances sit at zero.

Raises
------
ValueError
    If required grouping columns are missing, or the design is checked
    before any fit and refused with the setting to change: a constant or
    non-finite response, fewer than two genes, no gene with multiple
    guides, guides never replicated, more fixed-effect columns than rows,
    or linearly dependent fixed-effect columns. Also if no optimiser can
    fit the nested design.
spacr.cancellation.PipelineCancelled
    If the run was stopped; it propagates unchanged and is never reported
    as a fitting failure.
MixedBackendUnavailable
    If the selected mixed-model backend is unavailable.

Notes
-----
The statsmodels default optimiser runs first. If it raises or does not
converge, REML fits under ``lbfgs``, ``powell`` and ``cg`` follow. Only if
every optimiser raises on the full model is the guide variance component
dropped and a gene-only random intercept fitted; the record and the log say
so, because guides that disagree then no longer widen the gene interval.

spacr.qt.bridge.retire_live_work.canonical_text:
Stop every job runner and registered run within one shared budget.

The application's ``aboutToQuit`` drain and the interpreter's exit hook
both end here. ``aboutToQuit`` only fires when an event loop quits, so a
process that builds windows and then simply ends (a script, a test
subprocess, a capture run that returns early) never sees it, and the
QThreads its widgets started are destroyed during interpreter teardown
while they still run. Qt treats that as fatal. Whatever cannot stop in
the budget is parked, never terminated.

:param timeout_ms: total wait budget across every runner and run.
:returns: how many threads are still running afterwards.

spacr.qt.screens.organism_screen.canonical_text:
Explore organism guides and open the available image-analysis modules.

From Home, choose an organism to read its introduction, explore the cell
diagram and browse its assay tiles. These guide pages require no input files
and produce no analysis files. Drag the divider to give the information or
module pane more space; each pane scrolls independently. Hover over a diagram
component to read its description, select several components to keep them
highlighted, and use Clear components to reset the selection.

.. _spacr.qt.screens.organism_screen.toxoplasma:

Toxoplasma
----------
Open Home > Toxoplasma and choose Plaque Assay, Recruitment, Host–Pathogen,
Invasion Assay or Replication Assay. The selected module provides its input
selectors, settings, preview and Run controls. Use its Test data control when
an example is available. Plaque Assay starts with images; the other assays
use the corresponding measurement tables and object relationships. Follow

spacr.qt.theme.make_transparent.canonical_text:
Stop ``widgets`` painting a background of their own.

A backdrop — the theme's wallpaper, or the DNA rain on the
sequencing screen — is behind the *page*, and in the opaque themes
every container between it and the eye is an opaque ``bg`` by
virtue of the blanket ``QWidget`` rule. One container is enough to
bury it: a screen's header widget, its splitter, a scroll area and
that scroll area's viewport are each a QWidget, and each one used to
paint solid black over the animation the screen had just installed.

Tag the layout containers with this and the backdrop reaches the
eye; leave the cards, panels and inputs alone and they stay the
readable surface on top of it. Safe to call on a widget that is
already visible — the style is re-polished so the change takes
effect immediately rather than at the next theme switch. A widget no
stylesheet reaches yet, or one in a window whose sheet is held
(:func:`_one_sheet_for`), is only tagged: nothing reads the tag until
a sheet arrives, and putting a sheet on polishes every widget it
reaches. Glassing Preferences tags about 400 containers, and polishing
each one before its sheet went on cost 53-64 ms for nothing.

A ``QScrollArea``'s ``viewport()`` is tagged automatically along
with it: they are two widgets, the viewport is the one that
actually paints, and forgetting it is the obvious way to get this
wrong.

spacr.qt.widgets.ambient.AmbientWidget.s.canonical_text:
Stop ticking and retire the shading thread. Costs exactly nothing
while stopped — no timer, no thread, and no frame held in memory.

Dropping the published frame matters because these screens stay
built: a dozen module screens the user has visited would otherwise
each keep a slot warm behind a tab nobody is on, which is 2 MiB apiece
for the aurora. The next :meth:`start` shades a replacement before it
starts the thread, so there is nothing to show for it.

The one exception is a backdrop that stops while it is still on
screen -- a CPU-heavy run pausing the animation
(:func:`_animation_paused_for_work`), reduced motion, or the
animation switched off. Its frame on screen is kept as the still
(:meth:`_paint_still`), because every console line and figure the
window paints over it asks it for a whole frame again, and shading
that frame on the GUI thread against the run's worker took 250-350 ms
on lesson 08's Measure run. Hidden, it keeps nothing.

spacr.qt.widgets.loading_screen.BlowAway.canonical_text:
The motion of the photomosaic's tiles as a wind front blows them away.

Pure arithmetic on arrays, with no Qt: every tile's launch time and flight
are drawn once from a seeded generator, and :meth:`frame` evaluates the
whole flock at one moment, so the motion depends on elapsed time only and
never on how many frames were drawn.

The front sweeps across the mosaic along ``wind``. As it reaches a tile,
the tile lifts towards the viewer, turns over like a card (one axis scaled
through the cosine of its flip angle, with a skew and a little
foreshortening for perspective), spins, and flies downwind with random
turbulence and slight gravity while it fades. Background tiles do not
fly; they leave with the front.

:param occupied: ``grid x grid`` booleans; ``True`` tiles fly.
:param origin: the mosaic's top-left corner, in widget coordinates.
:param side: the mosaic's side, in the same units.
:param seed: seed of the randomness.
:param wind: direction the wind blows, ``(x, y)``; down-screen is ``+y``.
:param start: seconds before the front reaches the first tile.
:param sweep: seconds the front takes to cross the mosaic.
:param pace: how many times slower than the 694 flight each tile flies
    (lift, flip, spin, travel and fade are stretched alike).
:param end: when given, the last tile has gone by then: lives are cut
    to end there and :attr:`duration` is ``end``.

spacr.umap_search.walk_clusters.canonical_text:
Try HDBSCAN scales on one map and return them best-first.

This is the clustering half of the ParaScape-style walk.  It can run for
every UMAP trial as that trial arrives, or later against the table row the
user chose. Duplicate and out-of-range candidate sizes are skipped; if no
size is meaningful the call is refused rather than fabricating a
one-cluster winner. A clustering failure propagates, while an undefined
silhouette is retained as ``nan`` and ranks below every measured score.

:param embedding: fixed finite 2-D or 3-D coordinates to cluster at each
    candidate scale.
:param min_cluster_sizes: candidate HDBSCAN minimum cluster sizes.
:param min_samples: optional HDBSCAN core-sample threshold passed to every
    candidate.
:returns: scored partitions ordered best-first, then by cluster size.
:raises ValueError: when the map or candidate sequence is invalid.

spacr.ml.fit_mixed_model.historical_english_text_for_existing_cat:
Fit a mixed model with guides nested within genes.

The model treats genes as fixed effects and guides as random effects
nested within genes. In statsmodels notation, ``groups=gene`` supplies the
outer random intercept and ``vc_formula={'grna': '0 + C(grna)'}`` supplies
the guide-within-gene variance component.

A blockable ``screenID`` supplied by :func:`prepare_formula` remains a
fixed effect. With only two screen levels, a random screen variance would
be estimated from one degree of freedom. The plate is not nested within
the screen because plate position is already represented by the row and
column structure. Single-screen data omit the constant screen term to
avoid a rank-deficient design.

Parameters
----------
df : pandas.DataFrame
    Model data containing the formula variables and the gene and guide
    grouping columns.
formula : str
    Fixed-effects formula, normally returned by :func:`prepare_formula`
    with ``level='gene'``.
dst : path-like
    Destination for the residual histogram.
random_row_column_effects : bool, default False
    Add row and column variance components instead of fixed terms.
gene_column : str, default 'gene'
    Column containing the outer gene groups.
guide_column : str, default 'grna'
    Column containing guides nested within each gene.
regression_backend : {'statsmodels', 'torch'}, default 'statsmodels'
    Mixed-model backend. The torch backend fits the same nested model
    with GPU acceleration when available.

Returns
-------
mixed_model
    Fitted backend-specific mixed-model result.
coef_df : pandas.DataFrame
    Fixed effects, variance components, and guide BLUPs. Variance
    components and BLUPs have ``NaN`` p-values because they are not
    fixed-effect hypothesis tests.

Raises
------
ValueError
    If required grouping columns are missing, no gene has multiple
    guides, or the backend cannot fit the nested design.
MixedBackendUnavailable
    If the selected mixed-model backend is unavailable.
